targets.text: jev-factory ships a distillery: Cloudflare Clef 27B labels a train split with per-option soft probabilities, Strands Decider 2B is benchmarked zero-shot, distilled (KL to teacher + CE to gold, LoRA), re-evaluated and assessed against both teacher and its un-distilled self, then quantized and healed once — every step a dry-run-by-default stage with recorded provenance and a pre-registered gate (issue #18)

The announcement holds only if a full 'jev distill' run produces the private bundle and both success signals (c42 on test, c43 on the quant) pass on the single final measurement; a run that misses either ships a failure report, not the announcement.

A teacher-label stage asks Clef over the SystemOne API (POST /v1/systemone) for every train-split item and stores the full per-option probability vector (soft label), not just the argmax, with provenance: teacher HF repo id, revision, quantization, serving engine, request config and a sha256 of each response.
A soft label is only stored if its probabilities cover every offered option of that question and sum to 1 within 0.01; otherwise the item is recorded as a teacher error, never as a label.

Benchmark stage: measure the teacher (Clef 27B) and the stock, un-distilled Strands Decider 2B zero-shot on the fit/selection folds through one scorer seam that consumes per-option probabilities directly, with no letter-token logprob readout.
The zero-shot benchmark of Clef and stock v21 runs only on fit/selection folds; a test or held-out file passed to it is refused.

A pointer-scorer student backbone adapter for Strands Decider 2B (Qwen3.5-2B-Base + LoRA r16/alpha32 + a separate pointer head in head.safetensors, pointer_dim 256, num_slots 24): prompt rendering, readout, trainer, merge+verify, predictions emitter, serve and quantize, behind a real backbone seam.
Stages that only need a distribution (calibrate, gate sweep, metrics, select, decide) import no backbone module; a test proves it for both the causal_lm and the pointer backbone.

Distill trainer: loss = alpha * KL(teacher soft labels || student) + (1 - alpha) * CE(gold) where gold exists, with per-question-kind distillation temperature, LoRA first; runs in the train venv as a subprocess under the GPU guard (run_gpu_stage).
With alpha = 0 the distill loss equals the existing gold-CE path on the same rows (regression test), and with no teacher target on a row the KL term is zero for that row.
Assessment adds macro-F1, JSD to gold, JSD to teacher, confident-wrong rate, log-loss and peak memory, each with bootstrap CIs, next to the existing ECE/reliability, Brier and latency metrics.
Each new metric (macro-F1, JSD to gold, JSD to teacher, confident-wrong, log-loss, peak memory) has a hand-computed fixture test and reports a seeded bootstrap CI.

A paired release gate compares the distilled student against the teacher and against the un-distilled student with bootstrap CIs on paired per-item differences, and an accuracy gain with worse calibration counts as a regression.
The paired gate resamples items jointly across student, teacher and v21 (same indices per resample), and a run with higher accuracy but higher ECE than v21 is reported as a regression.

Quantize the distilled student to its deployed format, re-measure it, heal at most once if the quant loses more than 3.0 points against its own bf16 (same trigger as the jev-tool path), re-quantize, and recalibrate on the deployed quant's own fit-fold predictions.
Heal runs at most once per distill run; a second trigger is refused with stop/escalate, and recalibration fits on the deployed quant's own fit-fold predictions.

Distillation has its own pre-registration (bars, selection rule, the teacher and un-distilled student as reference rows, and the knob grid: alpha, temperature, student size, data mix) locked before the first distill training command; any later change is a recorded deviation.
The distill train stage refuses to start without a locked distill prereg, and a changed prereg sha is refused unless a deviation id is supplied.

The teacher labels the train split only. Its soft labels never reach the fit/selection folds' training targets, and nothing from the sealed held-out or test side is ever sent to the teacher or used to build soft labels; teacher-labelled train rows pass the existing exact + near-duplicate leakage check, which fails closed.
The teacher-label stage refuses any record whose split is not train, and the leakage check runs on teacher-labelled and corrected rows before assemble, failing closed.

Test and sealed held-out are measured once: the teacher, the un-distilled student and the distilled student are scored in one final invocation (or the teacher's predictions are saved once and replayed), never as separate measurements.
A second final measurement of test or held-out is refused without a deviation id, whether it is for the teacher, v21 or the student.

Post-hoc jev-factory calibration (temperature, optional per-label vector) is still fitted on the student's fit fold; Strands' published per-kind temperatures (noul 0.818, choice 0.818, score 1.192) are upstream values or training-time distillation temperatures, never a substitute, and softmax confidence is never treated as calibrated.
The bundle's calibration.json is fitted by jev-factory on the fit fold; Strands' temperature_by_kind values never appear as the deployed calibration.

Every distill write step (teacher labelling, train, quantize, heal, upload) is dry-run by default with --apply to commit, uploads are private-first with fetch-back hash verification, and the base install keeps dependencies = [] (heavy deps behind the train extra, imported lazily).
Every 'jev distill' stage with side effects prints a plan and writes nothing without --apply (tested per stage); 'import jev_factory' with torch/transformers blocked still succeeds.

Upstream Strands hyperparameters are used only as a documented reference: any value taken from strands-decider's train_config.json or config is recorded as an explicit knob in the run, never silently inherited.
Every hyperparameter taken from strands-decider's train_config.json appears as a named knob in the run's knobs/prereg with its upstream source cited.

The distillery's record is a /v1/systemone request body plus gold: {id, state, questions:{qid:{type: choice|noul|score, instructions?, criteria}}} with per-question gold {label, probabilities?} for choice, {score level, probabilities?} for score and {probability_true} for noul, plus split and source/licence metadata. Teacher soft labels are stored keyed by (record id, question id), never by row position.
A typed-decisions row and a jev-bench row both round-trip through the record loader into the same schema, and a tool domain renders as one choice question whose criteria are its verbs.

The vendor 'confidence' field is never used as a probability or a gate input: it is defined differently per model (CLM: top minus mean of rest; Jev choice: (pmax-1/K)/(1-1/K)). Only per-option probabilities are read, then calibrated.
No code path reads the response 'confidence' field; a test asserts gate inputs derive only from 'probabilities' (or noul P(true)).

A distill knob selects which rows carry a teacher target: all train rows, or only rows where the teacher's argmax agrees with gold (Strands' v21 recipe); rows without a teacher target train on gold CE only. The choice is pre-registered and recorded per row.
The agree-with-gold filter is a pre-registered knob, and each training row records whether it carries a teacher target and why.

The distillery supports a correction dataset between Clef 27B and Strands Decider 2B, for domains where Clef is weaker or outdated: corrected targets sit between the teacher's soft labels and the student's training rows.
For any (record, question) with an approved correction, the training target comes from the correction, not from Clef, and the row cites the correction id.

Teacher trust is measured per domain/source before distilling: a teacher-audit pass scores Clef against human-labelled gold on the train side (accuracy, log-loss, ECE per source); where it falls below a pre-registered floor, that domain is flagged 'teacher-weak' and its rows take corrected or gold-only targets instead of Clef's soft labels. Sources whose gold is itself model-generated are not used to flag Clef.
The teacher audit runs on train-side items only and writes a per-source table (n, accuracy, log-loss, ECE) before any soft label is used; the teacher-weak floor is pre-registered.

Correction records have one precedence order, recorded per (record id, question id): human/operator correction > public human gold (e.g. jev-bench soft_label vote shares, typed-decisions gold) > an alternative teacher's soft labels > Clef's soft labels. Each training target says which source won and why.
Exactly one target source wins per (record, question), and the chosen source and the precedence rule applied are written on the row.

Corrections are train-side only, carry provenance (author or source, date, reason: weak or outdated), pass the same exact + near-duplicate leakage check against the fit/selection, test and sealed held-out sides, and are never derived from protected-side items.
A correction whose text exactly or near-duplicates a fit/selection, test or held-out item is refused, and a correction without author/source, date and reason is refused.

Agent- or teacher-drafted corrections enter as proposed and need operator review before they can train, through the existing 'jev review' seed-review flow (dry-run, --serve, --apply), and the review file is the record.
An unreviewed (proposed) correction never reaches assemble; only operator-approved or operator-edited corrections train, and the review file records each decision.

The operator, who runs 'jev distill' on the DGX Spark to turn a large teacher into a small calibrated student; and lobes' 'decider' role plus the mesh callers behind it (routing, triage, guardrails), which consume the distilled Strands Decider 2B over /v1/systemone.
The spec names both consumers, and the bundle serves on lobes' /v1/systemone wire unchanged.

Today the mesh's best typed-decision model, Clef 27B, needs a 4-bit 18+ GB build and one heavy-lobe slot; the stock Strands Decider 2B is fast and fits any box but trails Clef on accuracy and calibration; and jev-factory can only train letter-token causal-LM scorers with CE on gold, with no soft labels, no /v1/systemone scorer and no typed-question data contract.
The before-state facts are checkable: no soft-label/KL/systemone code exists in jev_factory at the base commit, and backbones/ holds only causal_lm.

Distilling keeps most of Clef's accuracy and calibration at 2B cost, so every mesh member can answer typed decisions locally and escalate to Clef or cortex only when the calibrated student is unsure; and the factory gains a reusable teacher->student path for any domain in the public decision format.
The success signals measure the claimed benefit: latency and accuracy/calibration are reported for student, v21 and Clef on the same box and items.

'jev distill' takes a public /v1/systemone-format dataset through teacher audit, teacher labelling, operator-reviewed corrections, a zero-shot benchmark, distill training, selection, quantize/heal-once, recalibration and one final measurement, and produces a private bundle of a distilled Strands Decider 2B with calibration, its gate, the data it trained on (with every target's source), and a report comparing it with Clef and with stock v21.
A full dry-run of every 'jev distill' stage on the toy fixture passes end to end, and an --apply run on a tiny fixture produces a bundle with all listed files.

On the final test side, measured once, against human-labelled gold from clean (non-overlapping) sources: the distilled student's accuracy beats stock v21 with the paired-bootstrap 95% CI of the difference above 0 and closes >= 50% of the v21-to-Clef accuracy gap; its calibrated ECE is <= 0.10 and no worse than v21's; its confident-wrong rate is no worse than v21's; and its median decision latency is <= 1/5 of Clef's on the same box. typed-decisions agreement is reported, not gated. The thresholds are pre-registered before the first distill training command.
Thresholds in the success signal are written into the distill prereg before training, and the final report computes each one from the single final measurement.
The deployed quantized student stays within 3.0 accuracy points of its own bf16 after at most one heal round, and its recalibrated ECE is <= 0.10.
The heal count and the quant-vs-bf16 delta are read from stage manifests, not re-measured on test.

The distilled student's bundle is loadable unmodified by 'strands-decider serve' (the hobson-hf-export/1 layout: LoRA adapter, head.safetensors, strands_decider_config.json, provenance.json), because lobes serves the 2B through that package and passes /v1/systemone through unchanged.
A test loads the produced bundle with the pinned strands-decider package in its own venv and answers a choice, a noul and a score question over /v1/systemone on 127.0.0.1.

A contamination check runs before the benchmark: every evaluation source (jev-bench config, typed-decisions workflow, JevBench) is compared with the public datasets listed in v21's training data and with Clef's published eval suites; overlapping sources are flagged and reported separately, never pooled silently into the headline v21 or Clef comparison.
The final report has a per-source table marking each source clean/overlapping with v21 training data, and headline numbers are computed on clean sources only unless the prereg says otherwise.

Teacher, student runtime and distill trainer each run in their own pinned environment, reached over HTTP or as a subprocess: Clef's card needs transformers 5.10.2 and torch 2.11, strands-decider 0.1.0 needs transformers>=5.15,<6, and jev-factory's train extra pins transformers 5.5.0, so none can share one venv.
Each environment's lockfile or image digest is recorded in the run's provenance, and a test asserts the base 'jev_factory' import pulls in none of them.

Remote model code is pinned and contained: Clef's joint_schema_model.py and the strands-decider package run only at a pinned HF commit sha / package version with hash, inside their own environment, serving on 127.0.0.1 only (strands-decider serve has no auth); the pins are recorded in provenance.
Starting a teacher or student server with an unpinned revision or a non-localhost bind is refused (reusing measure/preflight.require_localhost).

Before training, the distillery pins and verifies the student's inputs: Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B-Base at an explicit revision, the v21 repo at a commit sha, and v21's adapter_sha256/head_sha256 from its provenance.json; a mismatch fails closed.
Tampering with one byte of a cached head.safetensors makes the distill train stage refuse with a hash-mismatch error.

Records whose rendered state + questions exceed the student's 4096-token window are filtered before training and evaluation with a per-source count, or recorded as student-ineligible, never silently truncated; the pointer head itself has no option-count cap.
The assemble/benchmark manifests report, per source, how many records were dropped for length, and no record is truncated mid-state.
One distill run uses one teacher build: soft labels from a different Clef build (e.g. NVFP4 after 4-bit) are a new labelling run or a recorded deviation, never mixed into the same training set.
Assemble refuses a training set whose soft-label rows carry more than one teacher build id unless a deviation id is supplied.

Every 'jev distill' stage writes the same per-stage manifest and detached-job log that 'jev status' / '--watch' read, and teacher labelling resumes from its response cache after an interruption without re-asking answered items.
Killing a detached teacher-label run halfway and re-running it re-sends only unanswered items (cache hits counted in the manifest), and `jev status <work>` shows its progress.

tasks.summary: Typed-decision record contract and source loaders
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/records.py defines a record {id, state, questions{qid:{type choice|noul|score, instructions?, criteria}}, gold per question, split, source, licence} and validates it with named errors (unknown type, choice with <2 options, score with <2 levels, gold outside the offered options)

A LocalLLaMA/typed-decisions row (state/questions/gold JSON columns) and a Praveenrajus/jev-bench row (id, source, primitive, split, state, question, label, soft_label) both load into the same record schema; tests/test_distill_records.py round-trips one fixture row of each
A tool Domain (tests/fixtures/toy_domain) renders as one choice question whose criteria are its operations; gold is marked human or model-generated per source
Importing the module pulls in no third-party package; parquet input, if supported, imports pyarrow lazily inside the loader
tasks.instruction: New package jev_factory/distill/ (add __init__.py). Keep the record a frozen dataclass plus to_json/from_json; never key anything by row position. Fixtures go in tests/fixtures/typed_decisions/ (a few hand-written rows), never downloaded in tests. Mark gold provenance: typed-decisions gold is model-generated (a ~4B teacher's 3-sample mean); jev-bench labels are human (source datasets).

tasks.summary: Distill assessment metrics with bootstrap CIs
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/metrics.py computes accuracy per kind, macro-F1, JSD to gold, JSD to teacher, confident-wrong rate (pre-registered threshold), log-loss and Brier over typed-question predictions, each with a seeded bootstrap CI via core.metrics.bootstrap_ci
tests/test_distill_metrics.py checks every metric against a hand-computed fixture and asserts the CI is identical across two runs with the same seed
Score questions are scored on the level index and on the full level distribution; noul on P(true)
tasks.instruction: Reuse core.metrics (bootstrap_ci, ece, brier_one) rather than re-implementing; do not route through core.metrics.compute, which is tool-scorer shaped (expect_kind). Pure Python, no numpy requirement unless already a dependency. Peak memory is a measurement field filled by the benchmark/final stages, not computed here.

tasks.summary: Distill pre-registration schema and lock
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/prereg.py defines a schema-validated distill prereg: success bars (c42/c43 thresholds), selection rule, knob grid (alpha, per-kind distillation temperature, teacher_filter all|agrees_with_gold, teacher-weak floor, data mix, epochs, lr), reference rows (Clef, stock v21) and an upstream_knobs list where every value taken from strands-decider config cites its source file and key
lock()/require_locked() hash the file like factory.prereg; a changed file is refused without a deviation id; tests/test_distill_prereg.py proves both
A knob present in the run but missing from the prereg, or an upstream value without a cited source, is refused with a named error
tasks.instruction: Mirror factory/prereg.py's lock/require_registered pattern but keep a separate file (distill/prereg.json, distill/prereg.lock.json) so the jev-tool prereg is untouched. Seed the upstream_knobs example from strands-decider-2B-hobson-v21 train_config.json (lr 1e-4, head_lr 1e-3, 1 epoch, kl_frozen_weight 0.3, teacher_weight 1.0, ordinal_smoothing 0.1).

tasks.summary: SystemOne client and probability-only response parser
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/systemone.py builds a POST /v1/systemone body from a record and parses answers into per-question distributions over exactly the offered options, using only 'probabilities' (choice, score) and 'noul' P(true)

tests/test_distill_systemone.py: a fake server returning a deliberately wrong 'confidence' yields a byte-identical parsed result; a missing option, extra option or sum outside 1 +/- 0.01 is an error result, never a distribution
Non-localhost base URLs are refused via measure/preflight.require_localhost; the client uses stdlib urllib only
tasks.instruction: Use a stdlib http.server fake in tests (see how evals/providers tests fake providers). Record model id, request config and a sha256 of the raw response body on every result for provenance.

tasks.summary: Backbone protocol and registry, with an import-graph test
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/backbones/base.py defines the per-backbone protocol (render, predict distributions, train plan, merge/verify, export, quantize candidates) and backbones/registry.py registers causal_lm and pointer by name, importing each lazily

tests/test_backbone_seam.py asserts the distribution-only modules (core.calibration, core.gate, core.sweep_gate, distill.metrics, decide) import neither jev_factory.backbones.causal_lm nor jev_factory.backbones.pointer
Existing causal_lm callers keep working unchanged (full suite green)
tasks.instruction: Do not rewire the existing causal_lm call sites in pipeline.py/measure/release here; that is out of scope and would collide with other tasks. Only add the protocol, the registry and the import-graph test (extend the existing layering test style).

tasks.summary: Pinned environments and localhost-only server launcher
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/envs.py describes three environments (teacher, student runtime, trainer) by python path or image digest plus a lockfile hash, and records them into the run provenance
Launching a teacher or student server with an unpinned HF revision or package version, or a bind other than 127.0.0.1, is refused; tests/test_distill_envs.py proves each refusal
Importing jev_factory with torch, transformers, peft, strands_decider and sglang blocked via sys.modules succeeds, and pyproject dependencies stays []
tasks.instruction: Servers start as subprocesses (strands-decider serve; Clef via the transformers load_release_model sidecar or SGLang dev-clef image) with explicit pins from the run config; reuse factory/detach.py for detached processes and measure/preflight.require_localhost. Add run-config keys via factory/config.py KEYS only if needed, prefixed distill_.

tasks.summary: Student input pins and hash verification
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/pins.py verifies Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B-Base at the pinned revision, the strands-decider-2B-hobson-v21 repo at a pinned commit, and adapter/head sha256 against v21's provenance.json (adapter 59be987f..., head 0fc78684...)
tests/test_distill_pins.py: flipping one byte of a cached head.safetensors fixture makes verification fail closed with a hash-mismatch error naming the file
tasks.instruction: Work from a local cache dir; no network in tests. Upstream recorded its base revision only as 'inferred' (b1485b2f...), so the pin is ours and must be explicit in the run config.

tasks.summary: Run dataset build: licence filter, folds, sealed held-out, length filter
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/dataset.py builds the run dataset from typed-decisions and the Apache-2.0/MIT jev-bench configs, carves grouped fit/selection folds and a sealed held-out set from train splits (reusing core.split), and keeps each source's own test split as the test side

Records whose rendered state + questions exceed 4096 student tokens are dropped with a per-source count in the stage manifest; no record is truncated; tests/test_distill_dataset.py uses an injected token counter
Sealed held-out and test loaders expose only ids, counts and sha256, never text
tasks.instruction: The real token count must come from the student tokenizer in the pinned student env (subprocess); keep the counter injectable so tests stay CPU-only. Never use typed-decisions test rows or anything derived from predictions on them for training (its card forbids it).

tasks.summary: Contamination check against v21 training data and Clef eval suites
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/contamination.py marks every evaluation source clean or overlapping using a checked-in manifest jev_factory/distill/data/upstream_sources.json (v21's public training datasets, Clef's Decision Index suites) with the URL each entry came from
tests/test_distill_contamination.py: banking77 and clinc150 come out overlapping; an unlisted source comes out clean; the result is written to the run for the final report
tasks.instruction: Populate the manifest from the strands-decider-2B-hobson-v21 card's training data list and Clef's card/Decision Index suite list; cite each source URL in the JSON. Name-level matching plus an alias table is enough for v1; record that limitation in the module docstring.

tasks.summary: Teacher-label stage: soft labels on train only, resumable, with provenance
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/teacher.py sends every train-split record to the teacher over /v1/systemone and stores, keyed by (record id, question id), the probability vector, teacher repo id, revision, build/quant id, engine, request config and response sha256
A non-train record is refused before any request; an incomplete or malformed answer is stored as a teacher error, never as a label (tests/test_distill_teacher.py with a fake server)
Killed halfway and re-run, it re-sends only unanswered items and the manifest counts cache hits; it records whether questions were sent jointly or one at a time
tasks.instruction: Cache by sha256 of the request body like data/teachers.py cache_key, in its own cache dir. One teacher build id per labelling run; write it on every row. Default to sending a record's questions jointly (Clef's native mode) and record the mode.

tasks.summary: Correction records: schema, provenance and leakage-checked intake
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/corrections.py defines a correction {record id, question id, target distribution or label, author/source, date, reason weak|outdated, status proposed|approved|edited|rejected} and refuses one missing author/source, date or reason
A correction whose text exactly or near-duplicates a fit/selection, test or held-out item is refused using core.leakage; tests/test_distill_corrections.py covers both refusals
A drafting entry point turns teacher-weak rows into proposed corrections from an agent/model drafter, and never marks them approved
tasks.instruction: Corrections live in their own JSONL under the run; status changes come only from the review flow (next task). Keep the drafter injectable; the default drafter is an alternative teacher over /v1/systemone or the existing data/teachers TeacherClient.

tasks.summary: Pointer backbone adapter for Strands Decider (render, predict, bundle layout)
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/backbones/pointer/ implements the backbone protocol: predictions come from a pinned 'strands-decider serve' over /v1/systemone (via distill.systemone), never from letter-token logprobs
It reads and writes the hobson-hf-export/1 layout (adapter, head.safetensors, strands_decider_config.json, provenance.json) and refuses a layout missing any file
An integration test (skipped unless JEV_STRANDS_PY is set) loads a produced bundle in the pinned strands-decider env and answers a choice, a noul and a score question on 127.0.0.1
tasks.instruction: Do not import strands_decider in-process from jev_factory; drive it as a server/subprocess in the student env. Register as 'pointer' in backbones/registry.py (only that one line touches the registry).

tasks.summary: Distill trainer: KL-to-teacher + CE-to-gold, continuing from v21
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/backbones/pointer/train_distill.py (run in the trainer env) trains from v21 with loss = alpha * KL(teacher || student at per-kind temperature) + (1 - alpha) * CE(gold), LoRA, with every hyperparameter read from the locked distill prereg
A pure loss function has tests (skipped without torch): alpha = 0 equals gold CE within 1e-6; a row with no teacher target has zero KL; KL is 0 when student equals teacher
plan_train() returns the subprocess command without running it, and execution goes through factory.gpu.run_gpu_stage
tasks.instruction: Read strands-labs/strands-decider training/train.py and training/data/collate.py first and cite what you reuse (Apache-2.0 attribution). Whether to continue v21's own LoRA or merge then add a fresh LoRA is a pre-registered knob (frame park v6); implement both behind it. Ordinal score questions: keep ordinal_smoothing as a knob (park v2).

tasks.summary: Operator review of corrections through jev review
acceptance_criteria: jev review gains a corrections mode: dry-run plan, --serve on 127.0.0.1, --apply writes the operator's approve/edit/reject decisions to the corrections review file, which is the record
tests/test_review_corrections.py: a proposed correction is never exported as trainable; approved and edited ones are, with the reviewer decision cited
tasks.instruction: Extend jev_factory/review/ (core.py, server.py, page.html) without changing the seed-review behaviour; existing review tests stay green.

tasks.summary: Teacher audit: per-source trust table against human gold
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/audit.py scores the teacher's train-side soft labels against human gold per source (n, accuracy, log-loss, ECE) and flags a source teacher-weak below the pre-registered floor
Sources whose gold is model-generated (typed-decisions) are reported but never used to flag the teacher; tests/test_distill_audit.py proves both
The audit table is written before assemble can run (assemble refuses without it)

tasks.summary: Zero-shot benchmark of Clef and stock v21 on the fit/selection folds
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/benchmark.py scores Clef and stock v21 on fit/selection folds into predictions records with latency (median, p95) and peak memory per model
A test or held-out file passed to it is refused; tests/test_distill_benchmark.py uses two fake servers
tasks.instruction: Start and stop each server in sequence (one GPU job at a time, plan risk on GPU sequencing); record nvidia-smi/peak memory per model on the same box.

tasks.summary: Assemble the distill training set: precedence, filters, one teacher build
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/assemble.py picks exactly one target per (record, question) by precedence operator correction > human gold > alternative teacher > Clef, writing the source, rule, correction or teacher-build id and teacher_filter outcome on the row
Only approved/edited corrections are used; teacher-weak sources take corrected or gold-only targets; agree-with-gold filtering follows the prereg knob

It refuses mixed teacher build ids without a deviation id, refuses any non-train row, and runs the exact + near-duplicate leakage check against fit/selection, test and held-out before freezing with sha256 (tests/test_distill_assemble.py)

tasks.summary: Distill train, select and calibrate stage
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/train.py refuses without a locked prereg or verified pins, runs the knob grid through the trainer under the GPU guard, and selects on the selection fold by the pre-registered rule

Calibration (per-kind temperature, optional per-label vector kept only if it lowers selection-fold ECE) is fitted on the fit fold with core.calibration; Strands' upstream temperature_by_kind is never used as the deployed calibration (tests/test_distill_train.py)

tasks.summary: Quantize, heal once and recalibrate the student
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/quant.py spikes each deployed-format candidate (W4A16 torso + fp32 pointer head, ONNX int8/int4, GGUF torso + side-loaded head) and records the chosen format as a decision citing the measurements

Heal runs only when the quant loses > 3.0 points against its own bf16, at most once; a second trigger exits with stop/escalate; recalibration fits on the quant's own fit-fold predictions; heal count and delta are in the stage manifest (tests/test_distill_quant.py)

tasks.summary: Final measurement once, paired gate and comparison report
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/final.py scores Clef, stock v21 and the deployed student on test and held-out in one ledgered invocation (measure/once.OnceLedger); a second measurement for any of them exits non-zero without a deviation id

jev_factory/distill/report.py resamples the three models jointly per bootstrap draw, computes every c42/c43 bar from the prereg with n and CI on human-gold clean sources, reports typed-decisions agreement and overlapping sources separately, and records a miss as a miss
Higher accuracy with higher ECE than v21 is reported as a regression; latency and peak memory are reported for all three on the same box (tests/test_distill_final.py, tests/test_distill_report.py)

tasks.summary: Distill bundle and private upload
acceptance_criteria: jev_factory/distill/bundle.py writes the hobson-hf-export/1 layout with jev-factory's fitted temperature_by_kind in strands_decider_config.json, plus calibration.json, gate.json, the training set with per-row target sources, the comparison report and provenance; symlinks are refused

acceptance_criteria: tests/test_distill_e2e.py dry-runs every 'jev distill' stage on a tiny typed-question fixture, then runs them with --apply against fake teacher/student servers and a fake trainer, producing a bundle with every listed file
The e2e test runs CPU-only in CI without torch, transformers or strands_decider installed

tasks.summary: Operator run: distill Clef 27B into Strands Decider 2B on the Spark
acceptance_criteria: With the operator: the distill prereg is locked before the first training command; Clef (4-bit) and v21 are served pinned on 127.0.0.1; every stage runs with --apply; corrections are drafted and operator-reviewed; progress is reported every 30 minutes from 'jev status --watch'

The final report states pass or miss for every c42/c43 bar from the single final measurement; on a pass the private bundle is uploaded and verified, on a miss a failed-evaluation record is written and the announcement is not made
tasks.instruction: One GPU job at a time; stop the teacher server before training. Coordinate with lobes (orin-decision-models) on the bundle hand-off via the communicate skill. Any rerun of a final measurement is a /deviate record.

risks.text: GPU sequencing: a running teacher or student server is a foreign GPU process to assert_gpu_free, so benchmark, labelling and training must start and stop servers in sequence (frame park v8).

Ordering with the jev-tool build: the distill verb changes the jev-CLI domain's candidate set and surface sha; if it lands after the extraction plan's t34 freezes the seed, the jev-tool model trains on a stale candidate set (frame park v9).
Statistical power: about 400 typed-decisions test cases plus the human-gold sources may not resolve the >= 50% gap-closure bar with a tight paired CI (frame park v10).
Strands' training code (training/train.py, kl_frozen_weight semantics) was not read during the challenge pass; the distill trainer must read and cite it before implementing.
Per-option KL may be insufficient for ordinal score questions; ordinal smoothing is kept as a knob (frame park v2).
GPU memory on the GB10 for a 4-bit Clef 27B next to the ~34 GB already resident is unmeasured; labelling may need the resident model stopped (frame park v3).
Clef's joint scoring of multi-question records may produce different soft labels than asking each question alone; the labelling mode is recorded (frame park v5).
Whether to continue v21's own LoRA + head or merge v21 and train a fresh LoRA is decided by a pre-registered knob (frame park v6).
Detecting outdated teacher knowledge is not solved by the audit when gold is itself old; time-sensitive sources may need dated provenance (frame park v7).
The deployed format for the pointer student may not exist on every target runtime (Orin/edge); the quantize spike may end with bf16 as the only verified format (frame v1 decision).
Clef serving on GB10 is an assumption (c20): the transformers sidecar or SGLang dev-clef image must be proven on the Spark before the operator run.
Reusing jev decide's verdict set for distill runs is not planned; a distill-specific decide is a follow-up (frame park v4).

Clean human-gold headline may be thin: v21's raw training list (HF cardData, 29 datasets; strands-decider data/sources.md) includes banking77, clinc_oos, amazon_massive_intent, civil_comments, measuring-hate-speech, emotion, glue, boolq and more, which overlap most jev-bench configs; after excluding overlaps the clean human-gold test set (c42/c52) may be too small for the paired CI, so the operator may need to add clean human-labelled sources before t26 or accept reporting overlap-included numbers as secondary.

Selection runtime: the example distill grid is 96 candidates (alpha x per-kind temperature x epochs x lr x init_mode) and t18 has no per-candidate resume, so a full apply run is many GPU-days on one GB10 and any interruption retrains everything; the operator must shrink the grid before the lock and/or a per-candidate resume must be added before t26.
